stories.title: Deutsche Bank dismissed warnings about dealings with risky clients, reports claim
summary: International investigation using trove of leaked internal data allegedly shows German bank overlooked compliance concerns to safeguard profitsDeutsche Bank reportedly dismissed warnings about its dealings with risky clients, including high-profile Russian oligarchs, to protect profits, the findings of an investigation into a trove of leaked bank documents indicate.A leak of 15m internal files is reported to show that the troubled German bank repeatedly ignored concerns by its compliance officers about its risk-taking, despite having already been caught being used to launder billions of dollars for Russian criminals, spies and oligarchs between 2010 and 2015.

summary: Bank of America, Chase, US Bank, Wells Fargo and Truist were listed by users who have been experiencing issuesCustomers reported service outages and difficulty accessing their online accounts at several major US banks and the money transfer service Zelle on Monday after a technical issue at JPMorgan Chase caused ripple effects throughout the financial system.Chase said the technical problems were not a systemic issue and were not the result of a cyber-attack, and that it was working to bring banking services back online.

stories.title: The man with the golden touch: James Bond franchise is a money-spinner
summary: Big-screen debut of Ian Fleming’s creation in 1962, with Sean Connery as lead in Dr No, was start of marketing dreamNew James Bond announced ... and the name’s Pattinson, Robert PattinsonShare your thoughts on the castingPeter Bradshaw’s takeRobert Pattinson’s journey to James BondJames Bond may be 73 years old but the superspy holds a licence to print money, at the centre of an evergreen multibillion-pound franchise spanning blockbuster films, merchandise, licensing deals and sponsorship.The announcement that the Twilight and Batman actor Robert Pattinson is the next Bond comes seven years after Daniel Craig revealed that No Time To Die would be his last outing as 007.

stories.title: Several companies are using Trump tariff refunds for corporate bonuses
summary: Some firms are directing refunds to corporate leadership instead of reimbursing consumers, ProPublica finds Several companies that received refunds for paying Donald Trump’s tariffs have put those funds towards corporate bonuses instead of reimbursing consumers, an investigation from ProPublica has found.After analyzing securities filings and earnings calls, ProPublica identified at least nine companies who said they were receiving tariff refunds and noted they were directing some of those funds to their leadership.

stories.title: Americans relying on heating oil brace for harsh winter: ‘We’re often cold in our own home’
summary: Surge in prices is forcing many to cut back on spending, with a projected 21% increase in costs of those householdsMillions of homeowners in the US will pay hundreds of dollars more this winter to heat their homes as rising energy prices have pushed up the price of heating oil.The US Energy Information Administration projects households that use heating oil can expect to pay 21% more this year compared with last winter, with warmer temperatures expected to partly offset price increases.
